title: The server that fits six users
intro: Llama 3 70B on 4×80 GB. Memory reads 'full' at just six concurrent users. The GPUs were not cheap. Open the clues.

facts.label: Weights
facts.value: 140 GB, loaded once at startup — 180 GB should remain for KV cache.

facts.label: Real contexts
facts.value: Live conversations average ~2K tokens ≈ 640 MB of KV each.

facts.label: Allocator
facts.value: Each request pre-reserves one contiguous slab at max length 32K (~10 GB).

facts.label: Cache census
facts.value: Only ~25% of allocated cache slots contain real tokens.

facts.label: Between slabs
facts.value: Plenty of free memory exists — in gaps too small to fit a new 10 GB slab.

question: What's actually wrong with this deployment?
choices: The model is too big — quantize it and the problem disappears
Pre-allocation and fragmentation are wasting the pool — switch to paged, block-based KV allocation
Users send too much text — cap context length at 1K tokens
180 GB is simply not enough — buy four more GPUs
debrief:
The math says ~280 users' worth of 2K contexts fit in 180 GB — yet six fill it. Every clue points at the **allocator**: max-length slabs (over-reservation), 25% real occupancy (internal fragmentation), unusable gaps (external fragmentation). This is the exact 20–40% utilization finding that motivated **PagedAttention**: fixed-size blocks allocated as tokens land, one shared pool, no slabs. Quantizing or buying GPUs treats the symptom and keeps the waste.
